articles.title: In 2025, a 59-year-old former HP manager took a seasonal job in Antarctica; now 60, she wakes at 6:30, tracks cargo and dances under 24-hour daylight
articles.summary: Discover how May Lee transitioned from a 30-year career at HP to a seasonal job in Antarctica, embracing new challenges and the joys of life under the midnight sun.
articles.body: After nearly three decades working at technology giant Hewlett-Packard (HP), May Lee found herself facing a surprising career change in 2025. Laid off in February 2025, she initially looked for another job in the technology industry. However, after struggling to secure an offer, the former marketing and communications manager started exploring a different possibility: working in Antarctica, a place she had previously visited twice as a tourist. At 59, she secured a seasonal position as a supply technician at McMurdo Station, according to Business Insider. Now 60, Lee told the publication that her work life combined warehouse duties, a tightly scheduled day and an active social scene beneath the Antarctic summer’s persistent daylight.From an HP career to managing Antarctic suppliesMay Lee nearly spent 30 years at HP before being laid off in February. Despite having professional contacts and referrals, she reportedly struggled to land another job in the technology sector. The outlet reported that a friend of hers encouraged her to consider interests outside her established career. Her past visits to Antarctica made the continent an appealing possibility, and she applied for positions supporting the US Antarctic Program. Eventually, Lee secured a seasonal supply-technician position with Amentum, a contractor supporting station operations.At McMurdo Station, Lee managed a warehouse handling information technology and communications supplies. Her role included physical tasks alongside accurate record-keeping. Receiving cargo, operating a forklift, checking deliveries against database records and investigating inventory discrepancies were all included in her role. This job was a significant change from her previous career and required physical tasks alongside accurate record-keeping.A workday shaped by logistics in AntarcticaAccording to Business Insider, during her first season, Lee usually woke up at 6:30 am and prepared for a 7:30 am start. She described herself as a night owl who is accustomed to the comparatively flexible schedule and culture of Silicon Valley, making McMurdo’s fixed schedule an adjustment. The station’s “town hours” generally run from 7:30 am to 5:30 pm, Monday through Saturday, although schedules are subject to differ according to roles and operational requirements.Cargo deliveries are central to keeping McMurdo supplied. During Lee’s first season, large aircraft delivered supplies earlier in the summer, while changing conditions subsequently affected the type of aircraft used for cargo operations. In the warehouse, Lee received shipments, moved supplies, checked deliveries against database inventory records and investigated inventory discrepancies. Additionally, food availability reflects the challenges of supplying a remote station. Lee shared that lunch begins at around 11:30 am in the cafeteria, where residents can choose from options including pizza, burgers and buffet dishes. When cargo deliveries are in operation, fresh produce is more readily available. The resident described the food as varied and good, while also noting that availability can change as the season progresses.Line dancing and radio shows under the midnight sunAfter finishing her work around 5:30 pm, Lee reportedly completes her time card and heads to dinner. She described the station as having the feel of a small college town, where limited internet access can encourage residents to socialise in person. Their recreational activities include crafts, line dancing, art shows and other community events. This gives the staff opportunities to spend time together after work.Furthermore, Lee volunteers as a DJ, hosting a 1980s-themed programme called ‘Ms Purple!!’s 80’s on the 8’ on Ice Radio. Sundays offer a break from her usual six-day working schedule. She told the publication that she often sleeps late and sometimes nearly misses the station’s Sunday brunch. She sometimes uses the day for outdoor activities or to prepare for the coming week. Her unexpected move from a long career at HP to seasonal work in Antarctica shows how a surprising layoff can lead to a markedly different professional direction.You use AI every day. articles.title: From 2014 to 2021, Wisconsin tracked three permeable pavements through seven winters; concrete pavers froze less often and thawed faster below ground
articles.summary: A seven-year study by the USGS shows interlocking concrete pavers have fewer below-freezing days and thaw faster than pervious concrete and porous asphalt, suggesting they may help improve drainage and reduce road salt use in winter conditions.
articles.body: Winter is tough on highways in ways most drivers never notice. Water enters tiny cracks, freezes and expands, pushing the surface apart. The process can repeat when temperatures drop again. Cities using permeable surfaces to reduce flooding and pollution face another question: how do these pavements behave underground when temperatures remain below freezing?Seven winters of temperature data from Madison, Wisconsin, helped researchers examine how permeable pavements respond to cold weather. The US Geological Survey studied three types of permeable pavement: interlocking concrete pavers, pervious concrete and porous asphalt. The pavers had fewer days below freezing, higher temperatures during snowmelt, slower freezing and faster thawing than the other two surfaces. The findings were published in the journal Water in 2021.This is important, since ground that remains unfrozen is able to keep absorbing meltwater, rather than letting it pool on the surface and refreeze. That might ultimately mean less road salt; however, the researchers are quick to remind us that salt has its own set of concerns. The details of the experiment explain how the team came to that conclusion and where its boundaries are.How the test was set upIn summer 2014, researchers established three test plots at a research site in Madison, Wisconsin, next to an overflow parking area. The plots represented interlocking concrete pavers, pervious concrete and porous asphalt. Each plot covered about 500 square feet, or 46.5 square metres, and had an aggregate base about 21 inches, or 53 centimetres, deep beneath the pavement. An impermeable liner and concrete walls separated the plots from the surrounding ground and from one another. The adjacent conventional parking area was not one of the three pavement types in the temperature comparison.Temperature monitoring ran from 21 August 2014 to 6 July 2021, with sensors recording readings every minute. Each plot had 27 thermocouples arranged at three depths: immediately below the pavement and 15 and 30 centimetres below the aggregate base. No vehicles drove on the test plots, and no salt or sand was applied to them. Snow deeper than 5 centimetres was removed with a hand-operated snow thrower, while the adjacent parking area was ploughed and treated with sand and salt. The main comparison used 303 winter days when sensors in all three plots were working at the same time.What the temperature data showedThe main comparison covered 303 winter days with simultaneous readings from all three pavement types. The daily average air temperature was below freezing on 182 of those days. During those days, temperatures in the top, middle and bottom layers beneath the pavers remained above freezing on 42%, 68% and 81% of days, respectively. The corresponding figures were 20%, 38% and 74% for pervious concrete, and 25%, 45% and 74% for porous asphalt. These percentages are rounded summaries of the study data.Another measure counted days when the daily minimum air temperature stayed above freezing throughout the day. This occurred on only 39 of the 303 days. The bottom layer beneath the pavers stayed above freezing throughout the day on 263 days, compared with 214 days beneath pervious concrete and 212 days beneath porous asphalt.During the 120 days when the daily maximum air temperature remained below freezing, the top, middle and bottom layers beneath the pavers were also below freezing all day on 65, 35 and 14 days, respectively. The corresponding figures were 101, 82 and 35 days for pervious concrete, and 61, 58 and 28 days for porous asphalt. The porous asphalt top layer therefore had a similar number of frozen days to the pavers, but its lower layers froze more often.Researchers also examined three extended cold periods: the winter from late December 2014 to early March 2015 and two shorter periods in the winter of 2019 and 2020. During these periods, all depths beneath the pavers froze completely only once, while pervious concrete and porous asphalt froze completely during all three periods. Across the three pavement types, the top layer took an average of about 13 hours to freeze after air temperatures fell below zero. The middle layer took about one day and 15 hours, while the bottom layer took about three days and 22 hours. Thawing generally occurred faster than freezing, although the time varied by pavement type and depth.The researchers suggested that differences in construction may help explain the results. The gaps between the pavers occupy about 10% of the surface, while pores in pervious concrete and porous asphalt extend across their surfaces. The researchers proposed that the arrangement of the pavers, the movement of air and water through the gaps and aggregate base, and the thermal mass of the concrete blocks may affect heat transfer. These are possible explanations offered by the authors, rather than mechanisms independently established by the experiment. The darker, porous asphalt surface may also absorb more sunlight, helping explain why it stayed warmer near the surface than the previous concrete.What it means for road saltThese temperature differences matter during snowmelt. When the layers below a pavement remain above freezing, meltwater is more likely to infiltrate instead of pooling on the surface and refreezing. Researchers identified 137 melt days from meteorological records. Temperature data were available for 103 of those days for the pavers, 47 for pervious concrete and 89 for porous asphalt. On days with available data, the daily maximum temperature across all measured depths stayed above freezing on 96% of paver observations, 93% of porous asphalt observations and 83% of pervious concrete observations.The authors cited earlier studies reporting that permeable pavements could reduce road salt use. One study in Toronto reported about half as much salt use at a site with interlocking concrete pavers, while research in New Hampshire found that porous asphalt could maintain comparable or better surface conditions with 64% to 77% less salt than conventional asphalt.These findings do not mean that salt can be used without environmental consequences. Dissolved chloride can pass through permeable pavement and reach groundwater, even when the surface reduces runoff or the need for deicing. The researchers therefore recommended minimising salt use where possible and avoiding it when conditions permit.There are some boundaries to remember. The study was at a single site in one city, the plots were small, and nobody drove on them, so the findings reflect temperature behaviour rather than how well each surface handles traffic. The work was funded by various donors, including a foundation for teaching and research on interlocking concrete pavements, as well as Wisconsin agencies, the City of Madison and the USGS. The authors say the funders played no role in the findings. The findings suggest that all three permeable surfaces can retain temperature conditions that allow water to infiltrate during winter melt events, with interlocking pavers performing best in the temperature comparisons.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 2019, South Korean boy Leo Park began posting detailed drawings of buildings online; seven years later, at 16, his freehand art fills a 30-city British colouring book and has attracted over 500,000 followers
articles.summary: South Korean teenager Leo Park was just nine when he began sharing his drawings of buildings and streets on Instagram in 2019.
articles.body: South Korean teenager Leo Park was just nine when he began sharing his drawings of buildings and streets on Instagram in 2019. Seven years later, the 16-year-old has turned his love for drawing into a colouring book featuring 30 cities across the UK. Created in collaboration with British company Colour Your Streets, the book, titled Enchanting British Cities, brings together his hand-drawn illustrations of well-known landmarks and local buildings. It was released as a limited edition in June.According to Colour Your Streets' official website, the collection includes illustrations of Oxford, Sheffield, Cambridge, Manchester and Liverpool. Unlike a conventional travel guide, the book lets readers add colour to Park's drawings. Each page contains detailed architectural features, along with hidden emblems incorporated into the scenes.For Park, drawing buildings is not simply about recording what he sees. His sketches often contain changes to the original structures, reflecting how he imagines a place could look. A building might retain its recognisable design while gaining new features, or an ordinary street scene might be presented differently to emphasise its architecture.This approach has developed over several years of travelling, observing buildings and studying their history. In an interview with Hallyuism, Park discussed how his childhood interest in drawing gradually became a serious career ambition.Instagram sketches to published booksPark had been interested in drawing long before he started posting his work online. However, 2019 became an important year because it gave him an opportunity to show his sketches to people beyond his immediate circle. As more people began seeing his work, he started taking on increasingly complicated drawings.His Instagram account, @draw_vengers, also reflects another childhood interest. Park came up with the name when he was 10, combining his enthusiasm for the Avengers films with his interest in drawing.The account eventually helped him secure his first publishing opportunity. A publisher came across his artwork and approached him about creating a book. The result was Leo's Art Adventure in the United Kingdom: The Boy Who Draws the World, published in 2022.Park chose Britain as the subject because he had recently spent considerable time travelling there. During that visit, he had collected drawings and experiences that could be developed into a book. He had also met artists, writers and other people whose stories became part of the project.His publishing work has since expanded to include Leo's Fantastic Urban Sketch Coloring Book and the collaboration with Colour Your Streets.Why drawings don't always match realityOne feature of Park's artwork is that he does not consider an exact reproduction of a building essential. He sometimes sketches directly at a location, but the final illustration may include changes that are not present in the original structure.He explained that his choice of subject depends on several factors. Sometimes a building attracts him because of its appearance. In other cases, its historical significance makes it worth drawing.St Paul's Cathedral in London is among his favourite subjects. Park has drawn the building at least seven times and considers its architect, Sir Christopher Wren, one of the most important influences on his work.He also admires Italian sculptor Gian Lorenzo Bernini and Leonardo da Vinci. Bernini's ability to show movement in sculpture interests him, while da Vinci's practice of carefully observing his surroundings has influenced how Park approaches his own drawings.His interest in history can also be seen in sketches of Winston Churchill's statue in London and Napoleon's Tomb in Paris. But drawing human figures has occasionally presented difficulties. While working on Churchill's statue, Park struggled to give the figure the appearance he wanted. He eventually used hatching, a technique involving closely placed lines, to add texture.In one illustration, he combined Korean architectural traditions with the fictional world of Harry Potter to create a Korean-inspired version of Hogwarts. Other works bring together landmarks and references from films and musicals.A different education path to pursue artPark's commitment to drawing has also influenced his schooling. During his Hallyuism interview, when he was 15, he said he had completed middle school and decided not to follow the conventional high-school route.Instead, he intended to obtain an equivalent qualification through an examination, allowing him to devote more time to developing his artistic skills.His parents, he said, have supported that decision and his wider ambitions. Their encouragement has been particularly important because his work involves travelling abroad, which requires both money and time.Park had also discussed plans for an extended sketching trip across Europe, where he hoped to concentrate on drawing streets and buildings before returning to further study and practice.Although much of his work features European architecture, he has drawn the Taj Mahal on more than one occasion, including in 2022 and 2024, and has expressed a desire to visit India to explore its history and cultural heritage.You use AI every day. articles.title: Europe Spring? Protests engulf continent as people take to streets in France, Albania, Italy, Spain, Portugal
articles.summary: Thousands of people took to the streets across Europe over the weekend to protest against rising living costs, housing affordability, pensions, education
articles.body: Thousands of people took to the streets across Europe over the weekend to protest against rising living costs, housing affordability, pensions, education standards, alleged corruption and war, with demonstrations in several countries leading to clashes with police and tighter security measures.France, Albania, Italy, Spain and Portugal witnessed rallies on Saturday, with demonstrators raising demands ranging from action against government corruption and investment in education to protection of public pensions and access to affordable housing.Authorities deployed additional police personnel and, in some areas, soldiers after violence during earlier demonstrations. While several rallies remained peaceful, others saw protesters throw projectiles at police, set fires and damage property.France sees arrests as protests turn violentIn France, nearly 1,000 people had been arrested during Saturday's demonstrations, interior minister Laurent Nuñez said, adding that the figure was likely to rise further.The government estimated that 410,000 people had taken part in protests nationwide, while organisers put the turnout at nearly 800,000.Authorities in Paris announced that the demonstration along Cours de Vincennes had been dispersed following clashes between protesters and law enforcement personnel, France 24 reported.Police used water cannons and tear gas after projectiles were thrown at officers."A Gendarmerie helicopter has been deployed to support ground units and locate any remaining groups of rioters," the prefectural police said, adding that more than 500 people described as rioters had been present towards the end of the demonstration.French left-wing leader and presidential candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon criticised the police response, accusing officers of using tear gas and firing into the crowd at the back of the procession. He also alleged that media coverage was presenting the protest movement negatively.US President Donald Trump also commented on the unrest during a campaign rally in Perry, Georgia, on Saturday, blaming France's immigration policies for the situation.Albania protests see clashes with riot policeIn Albania, thousands of people gathered in the capital, Tirana, for another anti-government demonstration, with protests also spreading to other cities.Riot police used tear gas, water cannons and rubber bullets to disperse demonstrators who threw rocks at officers and started a fire at the entrance to the agriculture ministry, Reuters reported.Visuals showed protesters firing streams of firework rockets towards riot police and fireworks exploding.Protesters also targeted government buildings and banks, smashed shop windows and pulled up paving stones to throw at police.The student-led demonstrations have been fuelled by anger over alleged government corruption, unemployment and poor education standards.High school and university students have demanded lower tuition fees, greater state investment in education and action against corruption in the education system. Some have joined a wider movement calling for the resignation of Prime Minister Edi Rama.The unrest follows months of largely peaceful summer protests against a luxury coastal development backed by US President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner.Authorities deployed around 2,500 police officers in Tirana on Saturday. Protesters had hurled rocks, flares, firebombs and fireworks at police over the preceding week, while authorities said more than 300 protesters and police personnel had been injured.Italy deploys soldiers amid renewed demonstrationsThousands of young people marched in Milan, Rome, Turin, Naples, Bologna and Florence, with demonstrations focusing on a range of social and political concerns. Some protesters threw bottles, stones and firecrackers.Italian police said nine people had been arrested and 371 briefly detained during demonstrations in eight cities on Saturday. Of those taken to police stations, 110 were minors.In Milan, the march remained peaceful as authorities deployed soldiers and police personnel and several luxury shops boarded up their windows. Most shops had reopened by late afternoon.Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni announced that an additional 500 soldiers would be sent to Milan, alongside tougher penalties for minors involved in violence. Hundreds of soldiers were already stationed in the city, supporting around 5,000 police and other security personnel.Meloni thanked law enforcement personnel for protecting public safety and the right to peaceful protest."The right to demonstrate must always be guaranteed, just as the right of citizens to live their cities in safety must be," she wrote in a post on X.In Rome, a small group of protesters tried to force their way into the Colosseum but were ushered out by guards.A separate anti-war march briefly clashed with police near Piazza della Repubblica, with demonstrators retreating after officers deployed a water cannon, news agency AP reported.The latest demonstrations followed violent clashes and looting during protests the previous weekend. In Milan, shops in the fashion district, including luxury boutiques, had boarded up their windows in anticipation of renewed unrest.Spain rallies focus on pensions and housingIn Madrid, thousands of retirees and other demonstrators marched to demand protection for the public pension system and increases linked to actual inflation.Protesters called for higher minimum pensions in line with the minimum wage, measures to narrow the gender pension gap and safeguards against the privatisation of public pensions.As per reports, thereChaos on the streets was captured in several viral videos on social media.The demonstrations came ahead of a snap election next month. Spain's governing Socialist Party has criticised the conservative opposition Popular Party over proposals it says could open the door to privatising public pensions.Housing affordability has also been a source of discontent in Spain, where rental and home prices have risen in recent years beyond what many people can afford.Lisbon housing protest camp cleared by policeIn Portugal, affordable housing was a central demand as thousands marched through Lisbon on Saturday. Protesters opposed rising rents and living costs, arguing that housing had become increasingly difficult to afford, particularly for younger people.After the march, demonstrators pitched more than 100 tents in Rossio Square. Police moved in shortly after 2 am on Sunday to clear the encampment, charging protesters and making several arrests. Minor injuries were reported, although figures were not immediately available, Reuters reported.Hundreds had gathered at the site to protect the camp after police dismantled a similar encampment on Tuesday."We have an obligation to fight for what we believe in," said Vitor Gomes, a 21-year-old multimedia communications student, citing housing speculation, concentrated wealth and rising inequality as reasons for his pessimism about the future.Protesters called on the government to scrap a bill that would make evictions easier and remove rent caps on new leases. The legislation had passed its first parliamentary reading, Reuters reported.Portugal is facing a severe housing affordability crisis, with house prices more than doubling since 2017 and rents for new leases nearly doubling over the same period. The Bank of Portugal estimates that the country faces a shortfall of 300,000 homes.The protests across Europe reflected a broad range of demands, from education and corruption to pensions and housing, while clashes in several cities prompted authorities to strengthen security and step up efforts to prevent further violence.You use AI every day. articles.title: A Georgia family built an outdoor kitchen and pool pavilion without HOA approval; a dispute over the community’s design rules ended up before an appeals court
articles.summary: A Georgia appeals court has upheld an order requiring a couple to demolish an outdoor kitchen and pool pavilion built without homeowners association
articles.body: A Georgia appeals court has upheld an order requiring a couple to demolish an outdoor kitchen and pool pavilion built without homeowners association approval. Earl and Deidre Cotton constructed the 594-square-foot structure, which stood 19.5 feet high, despite design rules limiting detached structures on properties smaller than one acre to less than 120 square feet and 12 feet in height. The Vining Estates Community Association had rejected their plans and warned them to stop construction. On 6 May 2026, the Georgia Court of Appeals affirmed a jury award of $6,475 in unpaid fines and $73,000 in attorney fees, alongside the removal order.Why did a Georgia pool pavilion dispute reach courtThe Cottons lived in the Vinings Estates subdivision in Mableton, Georgia, where homeowners were subject to the community’s Declaration of Protective Covenants and the association’s architectural review procedures. Under the declaration, proposed exterior construction and alterations required written plans and approval from the association’s board or its designated representative. The rules also required detached structures to receive prior written consent and to remain consistent with the home’s design, materials and colours.On 23 September 2021, the couple submitted a request seeking permission to construct a freestanding outdoor kitchen and pool pavilion. According to the court’s judgment, the proposed structure measured approximately 594 square feet and stood 19.5 feet high. The plans included an enclosed bathroom, storage space, a covered outdoor kitchen and utilities, including water and electrical power. By signing the application, the couple acknowledged that construction would not begin until the association’s architectural review committee or board had communicated its approval.Why did the HOA reject the pavilion plansThe association’s design guidelines imposed specific limits on structures proposed for properties measuring less than one acre. Under those rules, permitted structures had to be smaller than 120 square feet, no higher than 12 feet and positioned in the rear garden within the extended sidelines of the house. They also had to use materials and finishes compatible with the home’s exterior, and utilities were prohibited.The architectural review committee rejected the Cottons’ proposal because it exceeded the permitted size and height, fell outside the specified location and included prohibited utilities. The association informed the couple that they could submit an amended application or appeal the decision. They subsequently appealed to the board and requested a variance, but their revised proposal did not change the structure’s dimensions or location and continued to include utilities. Although the couple later said the pavilion’s height would be reduced to a maximum of 15 feet, that remained above the 12-foot limit. The board rejected the proposal, noting that changes had not been made to the structure’s size.Why did the family continue building despite HOA warningsThe court record showed that the couple had already entered into a construction contract and purchased materials before submitting their modification request. Deidre Cotton also testified that construction began before the architectural review committee had reached a decision. When association representatives learned that work had started, they instructed the couple to stop until the proposed structure had been approved.James Funk, the association’s president, visited the property and warned Earl Cotton that continued construction could lead to fines and that the pavilion might have to be demolished. The property manager also told him that the committee was still reviewing the request for a variance and that work should stop in the meantime. According to the judgment, Cotton responded that he was “on the right side of this” and was “going to keep building”. On 28 February 2022, the board sent a letter demanding that construction cease and that the structure be removed. It imposed an initial fine of $1,500, together with a further $25 for each day the structure remained unapproved. The couple nevertheless continued building, completing the pavilion on 24 May 2022.Why did the appeals court uphold the pavilion’s removalThe association subsequently sued the couple, seeking unpaid fines, attorney fees and a permanent injunction requiring the removal of the pavilion and restoration of the property. After the case proceeded to trial, the jury found in favour of the association and awarded $6,475 in unpaid fines and $73,000 in attorney fees. The trial court then ordered the couple to remove the entire detached structure and restore the area to its original condition. The order was stayed while the appeal was pending, subject to a supersedeas bond of $230,000.The Cottons challenged several aspects of the proceedings, including the enforcement of the design guidelines, the rejection of their proposed structure and the trial court’s decision to grant an injunction after the jury had dispersed. The Court of Appeals rejected their arguments and affirmed both the jury’s verdict and the injunction. In its reasoning, the court noted that the couple had completed a structure they knew violated several requirements and had never obtained the necessary approval. It also concluded that they had not identified an adequate legal remedy or a less oppressive alternative to the injunction. The judgment therefore left in place the order requiring the pavilion’s removal and restoration of the affected area.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Iran claims downing US drone over Bandar Abbas after Trump hints at renewed strikes
articles.summary: Iran on Sunday claimed its air defence system had shot down a US drone over the southern port city of Bandar Abbas, state media reported.
articles.body: Iran on Sunday claimed its air defence system had shot down a US drone over the southern port city of Bandar Abbas, state media reported.The drone was identified as a Low-cost Uncrewed Combat Attack System (LUCAS), a one-way attack drone, also known as a kamikaze or loitering drone, developed for the US armed forces, Reuters reported, citing Iran’s semi-official Tasnim news agency.However, the report has not been independently verified.The arrives came after the US President Donald Trump hinted at the possibility of renewed military action against Iran as early as Sunday, while leaving open the possibility of a diplomatic agreement.Speaking to reporters after casting his ballot in Florida on Saturday, Trump said Iran wanted a deal to reopen the waterway but questioned whether Tehran would honour any agreement.“Do you really think I would tell you that? Maybe tomorrow... There's a possibility I will. There's also a possibility we'll have a nice, big, beautiful agreement,” Trump said when asked about the prospect of fresh strikes.Trump also reiterated his hardline stance towards Tehran at a campaign rally in Florida, warning that the US could launch another military operation if Iran failed to reach an agreement.“We may do another little Epic Fury, or they'll agree,” he said, referring to the previous US military campaign against Iran.On Sunday, Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi said a potential resumption of war with Israel and the United States would not change Tehran’s policies."Recently, there has been talk of a new war, but I am already thinking about the post-war period. Whether there is war or not, our policies remain the same," Araghchi said during a televised event in Tehran, AFP reported."They have already done so twice and have seen the results. If they want to try again, they know they will achieve no different outcome from those of the past," he added.Iran has claimed control over the Strait of Hormuz since the outbreak of the war and has regularly targeted vessels attempting to cross without its authorisation. The moves have drawn strong opposition from Washington and countries in the region.In response, the US has maintained a naval counter-blockade on Iranian ports, including strategically important Bandar Abbas.You use AI every day. articles.title: Tensions flare in Hyderabad after eggs thrown at Durga Mata idol during immersion procession
articles.summary: HYDERABAD: Tensions flared late at night after Hindu organisations staged a protest over an alleged incident in which eggs were thrown at a Durga Mata
articles.body: HYDERABAD: Tensions flared late at night after Hindu organisations staged a protest over an alleged incident in which eggs were thrown at a Durga Mata idol during an immersion procession within the Madanapet police station limits in Hyderabad.According to news agency ANI, police received information about the incident through a phone call, immediately reached the spot, took the suspects into custody, registered a case and are investigating the matter.According to a police official, "We received a Dial 100 call stating that some individuals had thrown eggs at a Durga Mata idol during a procession near Santosh Nagar hotel line, under Madanapet police station limits.""We immediately reached the spot, conducted an enquiry, registered a case, and took the suspects into custody. Currently, we are investigating the matter, " the police official added.Earlier, a similar stone-pelting incident was reported during a Durga Visarjan procession in Maharashtra’s Washim, prompting police to register an FIR, officials said.The incident reportedly followed an argument over the throwing of gulal (coloured powder). Police intervened and brought the situation under control, and officials said the area was now peaceful. articles.title: In 1894, a gold discovery turned Minnesota's Rainy Lake City into a boomtown; seven years later, it was abandoned after yielding just $4,500
articles.summary: In 1894, the discovery of gold near Rainy Lake in northern Minnesota sparked a rush of prospectors, investors and workers hoping to make their fortunes.
articles.body: In 1894, the discovery of gold near Rainy Lake in northern Minnesota sparked a rush of prospectors, investors and workers hoping to make their fortunes. Rainy Lake City quickly grew into a busy settlement, complete with hotels, shops, saloons and a school. However, the gold deposits proved less rewarding than many had expected. Despite years of mining activity and repeated attempts to increase production, the operation recovered only $4,500 worth of gold before closing in 1898. Within seven years of its incorporation, the once-promising settlement had become a ghost town.Beginning of the Rainy Lake City gold rushThe story began before Rainy Lake City existed. According to the National Park Service, prospectors had searched northern Minnesota for gold for decades, but an important discovery came in the summer of 1893.Prospector George W. Davis was exploring Rainy Lake when he found a vein of gold-bearing quartz on Little American Island, near Black Bay Narrows. Quartz is a common rock that can contain gold and other minerals. Davis collected samples that showed promising results, raising hopes that the remote region could support a profitable mining industry.As reported by Forgotten Minnesota, Davis initially struggled to secure the money needed to develop the discovery. He eventually sold the mineral rights to a group of businessmen from Duluth, who moved ahead with plans to extract the gold.The discovery attracted attention because earlier reports had already encouraged people to believe that northern Minnesota contained valuable mineral deposits. This time, however, investors were prepared to establish an operation rather than rely on speculation alone.Rainy Lake City grew rapidly around the mining industryNPS records that Rainy Lake City was incorporated on March 17, 1894, as development of the Little American Mine gathered pace. The settlement was established to support the mining activities taking place on the nearby islands.The town expanded quickly as prospectors, labourers, business owners and other newcomers arrived. According to Koochiching County's historical account, the population had reached approximately 400 by the autumn of 1894. At the height of the mining boom, around 500 people lived there.Its facilities reflected the expectations surrounding the gold discovery. The settlement had 3 general stores, 3 hotels, 2 restaurants, a hardware store, a barber shop, 5 saloons, a post office, a customs office and a school. A newspaper, The Rainy Lake Journal, reported on local developments, while a bank was established as the community expanded.Many residents lived in tents, covered wagons, log houses and simple buildings made from tar paper. Although the settlement was remote, its growing population created demand for accommodation, food, equipment and other essentials.The scale of this development showed how quickly mineral discoveries could transform an isolated area. Yet the town's prosperity depended heavily on the success of the mines, leaving it vulnerable if gold production failed to meet expectations.Why was extracting gold from the mines so difficultThe main challenge was the nature of the gold deposits. The gold at Rainy Lake was embedded in quartz veins rather than lying loose in streambeds and gravel. Miners had to break into solid rock to reach it.This method required considerable effort, equipment and money. Workers used explosives to create underground shafts and remove rock containing the mineral deposits. The extracted material then had to be transported away for processing.At the Little American Mine, the ore was taken by boat for roughly a mile to Rainy Lake City, where a 5-stamp mill crushed the rock into powder. The gold was then separated from the crushed material using mercury.NPS notes that the mill operated from 1894 to 1897. The operation commonly employed 15 to 20 men on Little American Island, including underground miners and surface workers. Miners received $2 a day, while labourers earned $1.50.These wages were only part of the expense. Owners also had to pay for machinery, transport and the running of the mill. The difficult journey into the region made supplying the operation more expensive, adding to the financial pressure on the mining companies.Several mining ventures failed to deliver the expected returnsThe Little American Mine initially appeared promising. Forgotten Minnesota reports that the gold-bearing material processed in 1894 was valued at around $30 per ton. The operation expanded, with a vertical shaft and underground passages developed to reach the deposits.However, the mine's progress was uneven. A dispute between the partners forced a lengthy interruption in 1895. Later attempts to restart production encountered further difficulties, including the discovery of lower-quality gold than expected.Other mining prospects opened in the surrounding area. NPS identifies the Lyle Mine, the Big American Mine, the Bushyhead Mine and the Soldier Mine among the ventures that attracted attention during the 1894 rush.These operations generated hopes of a much larger mining industry, but their results were limited. According to Koochiching County, the mine on Dryweed Island operated for only a short time, while the Bushyhead Island mine remained in production for about 2 years.The Little American Mine performed better than the other local ventures, but its owners still struggled to turn the discovery into a lasting commercial success. Changes in ownership and repeated attempts to improve production reflected the continuing search for enough gold to justify the expense.The gold rush ended and Rainy Lake City disappearedBy 1897, the Little American Mine was still attracting investment. A new company introduced a larger, 10-stamp mill and extended a shaft deeper into the rock in the hope of reaching richer quartz.However, the improvements could not save the operation. Mining at Little American Island stopped in 1898, after the total value of the recovered gold reached just $4,500. NPS notes that this amount was insufficient to sustain the costly operation.The closure brought the wider gold rush to an end. With the principal source of employment and business activity gone, Rainy Lake City's shops and services could no longer rely on the steady flow of miners and workers. The school and newspaper office closed as the settlement declined.The town had become a ghost town by 1901. The end of mining did not mean every trace of the gold rush vanished. Forgotten Minnesota reports that abandoned shafts and other excavations remain on Little American Island, although vegetation has grown over much of the old mining site.What remains of the Rainy Lake gold rush todayThe former mining area is now part of Voyageurs National Park, which preserves the natural landscape and historical remains of the region. Visitors can still find evidence of the Little American Mine, including the remains of vertical and horizontal shafts.The discovery also formed part of a wider period of exploration in northern Minnesota. Although the local gold industry failed to develop into the lasting boom that investors had anticipated, mining activity encouraged people to travel into the region and search for other resources.Koochiching County records that some former residents settled in Koochiching after the mines closed. The community later became known as International Falls, which developed into an important centre for the lumber industry.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: 'Can't use it to kill people': Musk admits restricting Starlink in Ukraine
articles.summary: Elon Musk has acknowledged that his company, SpaceX, restricted Ukraine's Starlink satellite internet service last week, after Ukrainian officials said
articles.body: Elon Musk has acknowledged that his company, SpaceX, restricted Ukraine's Starlink satellite internet service last week, after Ukrainian officials said connectivity issues appeared to have been resolved.In a post on X on Saturday, the tech billionaire accused Ukraine's military of violating the service's terms by using it for offensive drone strikes. However, he denied responsibility for simultaneous disruptions to Starshield, the US government-controlled, military-grade satellite communication system that supports Ukraine's drone operations and communications."Using Starlink, a civilian commercial service, for offensive drone strikes to kill people has never been allowed, nor should it be," Musk wrote. "Ukraine military violated Starlink terms of service and used it for offensive drone strikes to kill people. That loophole was closed last week."Musk had earlier denied deliberately restricting Ukraine's connectivity, which Kyiv said had hampered its ability to conduct defensive operations for more than a week. Ukrainian presidential adviser Serhii Beskrestnov described Musk's latest post as "very strange". Kyiv has not officially commented on his latest claim.The issue emerged last week amid broader tensions between Washington and Kyiv over Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil infrastructure. Restrictions affecting Starshield also raised concerns among Ukrainian military and government officials, with commanders reporting lost drones and disrupted missions.Musk maintained that the US government controlled any changes to Starshield, the military-grade counterpart to Starlink. He also defended SpaceX's role in supporting Ukraine's defences since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in February 2022.The episode added to tensions between Kyiv and Washington, whose relationship had already been strained by US President Donald Trump's reported deal with Moscow on Russian diesel imports, which Ukraine viewed as a betrayal.Ukraine's defence minister Yevhenii Khmara credited "direct dialogue" and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's diplomacy with Washington for the outcome, adding that what mattered most was "for our front, for the military, the work of drones, logistics and communications".Questions have persisted over who ordered the interruptions to Starlink, a satellite internet system developed by Musk's company that Ukraine has relied on for years to counter Russian attacks.Trump has said he did not make the decision, while also arguing that Musk should not be blamed. US Vice President J D Vance has hinted at White House coordination with Musk, while Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth have denied any involvement by the administration.The restoration of connectivity comes amid renewed diplomatic efforts to end the war. Russia agreed on Wednesday to resume three-way negotiations with the United States and Ukraine next month. On Friday, Kyiv and Moscow also agreed to a localised ceasefire around Oleshky, a war-ravaged, Russian-occupied town in Ukraine's southern Kherson region, brokered by US first lady Melania Trump.Meanwhile, fighting continued on the ground. A man was killed and two others were wounded in a missile attack on Lozova in Ukraine's Kharkiv region, local officials said on Saturday.In Crimea, Moscow-installed authorities in several Russian-occupied cities reported power outages on Saturday following overnight Ukrainian attacks.You use AI every day. articles.title: Stricter enforcement of laws needed: Experts
articles.summary: Conservation experts and archaeologists have called for stronger protection of Odisha’s Buddhist heritage sites at Ratnagiri, Udayagiri and Lalitgiri,
articles.body: Conservation experts and archaeologists have called for stronger protection of Odisha’s Buddhist heritage sites at Ratnagiri, Udayagiri and Lalitgiri, stressing the need for clearly demarcated buffer zones, stricter enforcement of heritage laws and coordinated management by the ASI and state agencies.Experts said protection cannot stop at the boundaries of the protected monuments and must extend to their wider archaeological and visual setting.Buddhist scholar Sunil Patnaik said clearly demarcated buffer zones were critical to safeguarding the integrity of heritage sites. “Heritage does not end at the boundary of a protected monument. Any construction or developmental activity in the surrounding landscape has the potential to affect the integrity and authenticity of the site,” he said.Pointing to Ekamra Kshetra in Bhubaneswar, which has remained on Unesco’s Tentative List since 2014 without progressing to a full nomination, Sunil said inadequate buffer zones and encroachments had been a major impediment. “Encroachments and the lack of buffer zones around the site are primarily why it has not been nominated so far,” he said.Experts also called for stricter enforcement of the AMASR Act and Rules, greater awareness among local communities and scientifically prepared management plans for all three sites.The plans, they said, should cover conservation, protection of the surrounding landscape and future archaeological excavations.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Bhubaneswar | Silver Rate in Bhubaneswar | Bank Holidays in Bhubaneswar | Public Holidays in Bhubaneswar | Petrol Price in Bhubaneswar | Diesel Price in Bhubaneswar | CNG Price in Bhubaneswar | LPG Price in BhubaneswarStay updated with the latest Bhubaneswar news. articles.summary: A money matter that stayed half-finished now takes shape. The Full Moon falls in Taurus, your 2nd house of income, savings and spending.
articles.body: A money matter that stayed half-finished now takes shape. The Full Moon falls in Taurus, your 2nd house of income, savings and spending. Mercury retrograde in Scorpio, in your 8th house, keeps loans and shared dues in view. Results arrive, and the truth comes out. Count what is in hand before you decide anything.Aries Career PredictionsA pay query, a rate review or a pending client balance may reach a clear point. Bring a record of finished work and one firm figure. A senior could respond to facts faster than to requests. Someone may reopen an old payment term, so compare it with the earlier email. Keep each agreed change in writing.Aries Love PredictionsMoney views may surface between you and a partner. One may want comfort, the other caution. Talk about the goal, not about who spent what. Couples can agree on a monthly limit for shared costs. Singles may notice how a new contact treats a bill. Steady habits say more than gifts.Aries Money PredictionsA full picture of income and dues may appear tomorrow. List what you earn, what you owe and what you keep, all on one page. A delayed amount may arrive, so note the date. Hold new credit and large buys until Mercury moves direct. And skip any offer that promises quick returns.Aries Health PredictionsThroat, neck and stomach may react to money worry. Comfort eating could tempt you in the evening. Keep meals plain and at set hours. Sip warm water. Rest your voice after long calls. And close banking apps early, since tired eyes misread figures.Aries RemediesTotal one week of spending and mark the items you will cut. articles.title: HR in Indian Navy
articles.summary: We officers perform HR duties from the very early period of our career.
articles.body: We officers perform HR duties from the very early period of our career. And yet, for many years I was unaware of this term called HR (Human Resources), which flows in the bloodstream of the Navy. After a few years of experience, when I learnt that the ACOP (career planning) shall now be called Assistant Chief of Personnel (Human Resource Development- HRD), my attention was drawn to the term HR.Navy accords much priority and importance to HR, and a vast organisational set up supports the HR system. All the aspects of HR – recruitment, training, staffing, promotion, discipline, welfare and post-retirement care are undertaken by the HR organisation of the Navy. The amount of time, money and manpower invested in the implementation of the various policies is significant, and in my opinion only a few organisations may match the Naval system. Only the Army and Air Force have a similar system. The reason to accord such high priority is to meet the critical aims and objectives of the Navy, which are to protect the nation/win the war/provide national security. All organisations invest in HR in accordance with the Aims and objectives of the organisation. The Navy objectives have nationwide ramifications and therefore require a matching policy of HR. Organisation At the apex under the Chief of Naval Staff, there are four PSOs (Principal Staff Officers) responsible for Operations, Planning & Administration, Material & Maintenance, and Personnel (COP). The COP (Chief of Personnel) is of Vice Admiral rank and reports directly to the CNS. Therefore, one distinct wing is responsible for the HR of the Navy. Under him, there are numerous senior officers, Directors looking after the various aspects of personnel management – recruitment, selection, manpower planning, training, appointments, promotion boards, disciplinary action, ex-servicemen affairs, pay and allowances, welfare, civilian administration, etc. A similar organisation exists at Command level where Chief Staff Officer (Personnel and Administration) reports to the Commander -in -Chief.Recruitment and selectionThe men are recruited through a wide network of recruitment centres spread out across India in order to provide opportunity to all the states. There is a written examination, physical test and interview. A separate directorate looks after these functions. The officers are selected through UPSC (Union Public Service Commission), which conducts a written test, and thereafter the various SSBs (Service Selection Boards) in various stations conduct screening, psychological test, group discussions, physical tasks, group tasks and interviews spread over three to four days. This system is unique to the Armed Forces and has withstood the test of time.Training The Navy has three Commands, two operational and one dedicated Training Command Headquartered in Kochi under a Commander–in–Chief who reports to CNS. The initial and subsequent training of officers and men is conducted in a planned and systematic manner by this command. The Training Command is the prime mover of ‘Human resource development’. All newly recruited sailors report to INS Chilka in Odisha for initial training, and after six months, when branches are allotted to them, they are transferred to the particular training establishments functioning in different locations such as INS Shivaji for engineering in Lonavala, INS Valsura for electrical in Jamnagar, INS Hamla for Logistics in Mumbai, INS Venduruthy for seamen training in Kochi. Thereafter, they have to undergo courses at every stage of promotion and return to training establishments periodically. In addition, they also do leadership courses and Management courses when they become senior. Training and enhancement of skills is therefore a continuous process.Officer cadets are trained for four years at the Indian Naval Academy built in Ezhimala, Kerala, from where they obtain a BTech degree in order to be technically proficient to deal with the capital-intensive Navy. Some cadets are also trained in NDA (National Defence Academy) at Khadakwasla near Pune for three years, which is an inter-service institute. Thereafter, they join the Indian Naval Academy for the final year. All cadets proceed to ships for further training after the Academy phase. Ships are stationed in Kochi only for training purposes and are part of the training command. Training of technical cadets is conducted in Shivaji and Valsura after the initial training in Naval Academy. After commissioning, all officers of the executive branch undergo a full one-year training at the various training establishments – Navigation school, Signal school, Gunnery school. Anti -submarine warfare school, etc. Officers thereafter return to these schools after three years for specialization as nominated and become specialist officers. It does not end here! In order to be promoted and seek command, all executive officers have to pass the Command Exam and Staff College entrance exam. Some get selected to undergo staff college at Wellington, Nilgiris, a very prestigious course. Technical officers enhance their skills by being sent to IITs for MTech. On promotion to Captain, officers undergo the Higher Command course in War College in Goa; later, some of them who are Admiral material go to NDC (National Defence College) in Delhi, a joint service institute. Officers and sailors also have to undergo training and OJT (on-the-job training) when they are appointed to new ships with different weapon systems. Therefore, in a career spanning 20 years, an officer is in training for about 4 years on average after being commissioned.Management of personnel – Posting, promotion, welfare A dedicated and distinct establishment- ‘Bureau of Sailors’ headed by a senior officer and assisted by many officers at Mumbai- looks after the posting, promotion, annual confidential reports, and post-retirement placement of all sailors. On board, all sailors are in various divisions in accordance with their specialization. An officer is nominated as Divisional Officer who maintains the service documents of the sailors under him and monitors their progress, leave, discipline and other matters. The divisional system in the Navy is the core strength of the service. The various heads of department initiate ACR (Annual Confidential Report) of the officers under them, and the Captain reviews the same. Not only the performance, but the choice of courses, transfer, etc are noted for consideration. The details of school-going children are noted for next posting and appointment.All sailors are given 60 days' leave and also casual leave. A system of leave encashment on retirement also exists. In order to provide continuity in station posting, criteria are implemented as policy so that the education of children is not hindered. Sufficient accommodation is available in each station, and though not all personnel get accommodation, the HRA is useful. Sports and recreation facilities and medical care are accorded primacy in all stations. Military stations are a big homogeneous family. There is a dedicated Pay Office and Pension Office to monitor and credit all pay and allowances in time. As part of the social security group insurance is provided to all, and it has a good savings element; provident fund, gratuity give support post-retirement. Housing, educational loans against insurance schemes, provident fund, and benevolent funds are available in reasonable terms.Post-retirement placement is assisted by the Indian Navy placement department. A large number of courses in universities and management institutes are available for those retiring, and financial assistance and help are also accorded. Navy foundation exists in all major stations, and the officers and families meet regularly. A separate directorate, DNV (Directorate of Naval Veterans) looks after all retired personnel. Medical facilities in Military hospitals and civil hospitals are also available.Discipline A separate directorate deals with all disciplinary cases, and at the Command level the Personnel department takes responsibility. Commanding Officers are delegated powers of punishment, and defaulters are marched to him every week, wherein sailors are brought to his table, and cases are dealt. In certain cases, summary trials and court-martials are also ordered. Under the Navy Act of 1957, certain fundamental rights of personnel are abrogated, such as freedom of speech and freedom to form associations, and these are strictly adhered to.All the above is structured to provide a formidable human force to counter, sustain and prevail upon an enemy in any hour of reckoning. Above all, it gives all personnel a career of immense satisfaction and dignity on which rests the humanity.Disclaimer: Views expressed above are the author's own.
